name: Hungarian Pork Goulash with Potato Latkes, Sour Cream & Dill (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer pork to a plate and set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
1 lb lean ground pork
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel, trim, and small dice carrots. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers. Add to the bowl with the carrot.

Return pan (with drippings) to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add carrot, bell pepper, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies have softened, 3-4 minutes. Transfer 1 cup of cooked veggies to another plate, along with 1 cup of the cooked pork, then set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ medium yellow onion
2 clove garlic

instructions.primary_message: Add onion and garlic to the pan with the remaining veggies. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is softened, 2-3 minutes more.

Return remaining pork to the pan, along with tomatoes, broth, and spices. Stir to combine the stew and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until stew has thickened slightly, 10-12 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes
½ cup chicken or vegetable broth
2 tsp paprika
½ tsp thyme, dried
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper
⅛ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Set a small handful aside for serving. Place remaining dill in a large bowl along with eggs, flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper, then whisk to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ cup all-purpose flour
1 tsp baking powder
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Peel potatoes; using a box grater, coarsely grate, then place in a colander. Using your hands, squeeze as much water from the grated potato as you can, then add to the bowl with the egg mixture. Use your hands to thoroughly combine the latke batter.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches (and adding more oil as necessary), use a scant ¼-cup measure to drop batter into the skillet, spacing scoops a few inches apart; press down with a spatula to form round, ½-inch thick fritters. Cook latkes, flipping once, until golden brown, 4-5 minutes per side. Remove to another plate.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide plain pork, veggies, and 4 latkes between plates. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide stew between bowls. Serve latkes on the side, topped with sour cream and reserved dill. Enjoy!
